title: 10 Best Denial Management Services for Mid-Sized Hospitals in 2027
summary: Compare 10 denial management services for mid-sized hospitals in 2027, including providers for clinical appeals, A/R recovery, and denial prevention.
body_markdown:
> The best denial management services for mid-sized hospitals do two things well: recover revenue from denied claims through payer follow-up, appeals, and A/R recovery, and prevent the next denial by fixing the coding, documentation, and eligibility issues that cause them.
>
>
> Most providers specialize in one side: some focus on denials recovery, while analytics tools focus on prevention.
>
>
> CombineHealth is the one platform that connects both — using self-learning payer intelligence to recover denials and feed validated patterns back into coding, CDI, and pre-bill validation, so recurring denials stop at the source. At a 400-bed hospital, that reduced coding-related denials by 75%.


The best denial management services for mid-sized hospitals help reduce denied claims, recover outstanding revenue,[automate payer follow-up](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/ar-follow-up-in-healthcare-rcm) , and prevent recurring denials.


Some providers specialize in complex clinical appeals, while others offer outsourced A/R recovery, denial analytics, or[end-to-end revenue cycle automation](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/ai-tools-for-revenue-cycle-management) . The right choice depends on the hospital's denial volume, payer mix, internal resources, and recovery priorities.


In this article, we've compiled the 10 best denial management services for mid-sized hospitals, comparing their capabilities across:


- **Denial recovery:** Payer follow-up, appeals, underpayment recovery, and outstanding A/R.
- **Denial prevention:**[Coding audits](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/ai-medical-coding-audit-uncovers-undercoding) , CDI, eligibility checks, and pre-bill claim validation.
- **Clinical expertise:** Medical-necessity, DRG, level-of-care, and clinical-validation appeals.
- **Delivery model:** AI automation, managed services, consulting, or a combination.

## 1. CombineHealth: AI-Powered Denial Management and Revenue Cycle Automation


[CombineHealth](https://www.combinehealth.ai/) is an AI-powered revenue cycle automation platform for hospitals, health systems, and physician groups. It automates denial categorization, payer follow-up, A/R recovery, and appeals while connecting these processes with medical coding, CDI, eligibility verification, and pre-bill claim validation.


Rather than managing denials only after they occur, CombineHealth identifies recurring denial patterns and uses validated[payer outcomes to improve future coding](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/ai-medical-coding-denial-prevention) and billing decisions.


Its platform supports the complete denial management workflow, from identifying outstanding claims and prioritizing follow-up to preparing appeals, tracking payer responses, and identifying opportunities to prevent future denials.


### What Sets CombineHealth Apart


Two factors set CombineHealth apart.


First, **it connects denial recovery with upstream prevention.** CombineHealth analyzes payer outcomes, including denials, reimbursements, and underpayments, to build[payer intelligence](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/ai-medical-coding-denial-prevention) . Validated patterns can inform future medical coding, documentation review, and pre-bill claim validation, helping hospitals prevent recurring payer-specific denials.


Second, **it automates work across the revenue cycle, not just denial identification.** CombineHealth supports payer follow-up, A/R management,[appeal preparation](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/top-denial-appeal-platforms) , eligibility verification,[autonomous medical coding](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/autonomous-medical-coding-guide) , and CDI. This allows hospitals to automate routine workflows while routing exceptions to review.


### Notable Results of CombineHealth


CombineHealth has reported the following outcomes across specific deployments:


- **75% reduction in coding-related denials** at a 400-bed hospital.
- **4% increase in captured revenue** at the same hospital.
- **5× more CDI opportunities** identified.
- **25% reduction in outstanding A/R days.**
- **Up to 70% faster appeal turnaround.**


### Case Study: 400-Bed Midwest Hospital


A 400-bed Midwest hospital implemented CombineHealth to improve medical coding accuracy, identify documentation gaps, and reduce coding-related denials.


By connecting autonomous medical coding with CDI and payer-specific requirements, CombineHealth helped the hospital achieve a[75% reduction in coding-related denials](https://www.combinehealth.ai/resources/customer-success-stories/case-study/ai-matched-expert-coders) , a 4% increase in captured revenue, and 5× more documentation improvement opportunities.


The deployment demonstrates how addressing coding and documentation issues before claim submission can improve downstream denial performance.


**Best for:** Mid-sized hospitals seeking automated denial prevention, payer follow-up, A/R recovery, and appeals without outsourcing their entire revenue cycle.


## 2. Aspirion: Complex Clinical Denial Recovery


Aspirion provides specialized revenue recovery services for hospitals and health systems, focusing on complex clinical denials, difficult appeals, and underpaid or previously exhausted claims.


Its services cover medical-necessity denials, clinical validation, level-of-care disputes, DRG denials, government and commercial payer claims, and second-level appeals. Aspirion combines clinical, coding, and legal expertise with technology-assisted workflows to pursue challenging claims.


**Best for:** Mid-sized hospitals with high-value clinical denials, complex appeals, and aged claims requiring specialized recovery expertise.


## 3. EnableComp: Complex Claims and Denial Management


EnableComp provides technology-enabled revenue cycle services specializing in complex claims and reimbursement recovery. Its e360 platform supports specialized teams managing difficult payer and claim categories.


EnableComp's services cover medical-necessity denials, DRG downgrades, emergency department downgrades, coordination-of-benefits disputes, workers' compensation, motor vehicle accident claims, Veterans Affairs claims, out-of-state Medicaid, and underpayments.


**Best for:** Hospitals managing complex claims and specialized denial categories that require more extensive investigation and payer expertise than routine A/R follow-up.


## 4. AGS Health: Clinical and Administrative Denial Management


AGS Health provides technology-enabled revenue cycle management services for hospitals, health systems, and healthcare organizations. Its offerings combine managed operational teams with automation and analytics.


AGS Health supports clinical and administrative denial management, medical-necessity and level-of-care reviews, clinical appeals, payer follow-up, coding, CDI, prior authorization, payment variance analysis, and underpayment recovery.


**Best for:** Mid-sized hospitals requiring scalable operational support across clinical denials, administrative denials, coding, and accounts receivable.


## 5. Healthrise: Denial Analytics and Revenue Cycle Improvement


Healthrise provides revenue cycle consulting, operational improvement, and denial analytics services for healthcare organizations. Its approach focuses on identifying denial root causes and improving existing hospital workflows.


Healthrise supports denial performance assessments, payer trend analysis, account prioritization, workflow redesign, EHR-transition support, and denial-prevention programs. Its consulting-led model works alongside hospital revenue cycle teams rather than requiring full operational outsourcing.


**Best for:** Hospitals that want to retain internal denial management teams while improving analytics, workflows, and denial-prevention performance.


## 6. CorroHealth: Clinical and Coding-Related Denial Management


CorroHealth provides clinically focused revenue cycle technology and services for hospitals and health systems. Its offerings connect denial management with clinical documentation, medical coding, utilization management, and revenue integrity.


CorroHealth supports clinical-validation denials, medical-necessity appeals, DRG downgrades, coding-related denials, CDI, clinical appeals, and denial root-cause analysis.


**Best for:** Hospitals with frequent clinical, coding, documentation, and medical-necessity denials that require specialized clinical revenue cycle expertise.


## 7. GeBBS Healthcare Solutions: Coding and Denial Recovery Services


GeBBS Healthcare Solutions provides outsourced revenue cycle management services covering medical coding, billing, denial management, clinical appeals, and accounts receivable.


Its services include denial identification and resolution, coding audits, medical-necessity appeals, claim submission, payer follow-up, payment posting, underpayment recovery, and extended business-office support.


GeBBS combines coding and billing operations with denial recovery, making it relevant for hospitals experiencing denials associated with coding errors, documentation issues, and limited operational capacity.


**Best for:** Mid-sized hospitals seeking outsourced coding, billing, denial recovery, and A/R services from a single provider.


## 8. Omega Healthcare: High-Volume Denial and A/R Management


Omega Healthcare provides technology-enabled revenue cycle management services that combine operational teams with automation to support large-scale billing and collections workflows.


Its capabilities include denial processing, appeal preparation, payer follow-up, A/R recovery, medical coding, documentation support, eligibility verification, authorization services, and performance reporting.


Omega Healthcare focuses on improving operational throughput and managing high-volume revenue cycle workloads.


**Best for:** Hospitals with large denial backlogs, growing aged receivables, and insufficient internal capacity for timely payer follow-up and appeals.


## 9. TruBridge: Denial Management for Community Hospitals


TruBridge provides revenue cycle management services and technology for community hospitals, rural healthcare organizations, and regional health systems.


Its services cover denial management, appeals, A/R recovery, medical billing, coding, patient financial services, RCM outsourcing, and focused revenue cycle improvement projects.


TruBridge's focus on community healthcare organizations makes it relevant for hospitals with smaller billing teams and limited resources for managing complex payer requirements.


**Best for:** Community and regional hospitals seeking practical denial management, billing, and A/R support without building a large internal RCM operation.


## 10. FinThrive: Denial Analytics and Workflow Automation


FinThrive provides revenue cycle management technology and services designed to improve financial performance across hospitals and health systems.


Its capabilities include denial and underpayment analytics, pre-submission denial-risk detection, root-cause analysis, automated work routing, appeal workflows, claims management, A/R recovery, and cross-facility reporting.


FinThrive combines technology-led denial prevention with operational recovery support, helping hospitals identify recurring issues and prioritize outstanding claims.


**Best for:** Hospitals with established internal RCM teams seeking stronger denial analytics, workflow automation, and targeted A/R recovery capabilities.


## How to Choose a Denial Management Service for Your Hospital


When evaluating denial management services, focus on the work each provider performs and its measurable impact on reimbursement.


Consider the following:


1. **Denial coverage:** Clinical, administrative, coding, eligibility, authorization, and medical-necessity denials.
2. **Recovery capabilities:** Payer follow-up, appeal preparation, submission, underpayment recovery, and A/R management.
3. **Denial prevention:** Root-cause analysis, coding audits, CDI, and pre-bill claim validation.
4. **Integration:** Compatibility with existing EHR, billing, and payer workflows.
5. **Delivery model:** AI automation, managed services, consulting, or a combination.
6. **Financial outcomes:** Recovered revenue, denial reduction, appeal overturn rates, and days in A/R.
7. **Implementation and pricing:** Deployment requirements, internal staffing, fees, and time to measurable ROI.


The service agreement should clearly define which activities the vendor performs and which remain with hospital staff.


## **FAQs**


### **1. Does CombineHealth handle appeals and A/R follow-up for mid-sized hospitals?**


Yes. CombineHealth automates payer follow-up and A/R recovery, prioritizes outstanding claims, and prepares appeals with the supporting documentation attached. In deployments, it has reduced outstanding A/R days by 25% and cut appeal turnaround time by up to 70%.


### **2. What do hospital denial management services handle?**


Denial management services identify denied claims, categorize denial reasons, contact payers, correct claims, prepare and submit appeals, track deadlines, and recover outstanding revenue. Some also provide coding audits, clinical reviews, underpayment recovery, and denial-prevention analytics.


### **3. How does CombineHealth prevent denials, not just recover them?**


CombineHealth analyzes payer outcomes — denials, reimbursements, and underpayments — to build payer intelligence, then feeds validated patterns back into coding, documentation review, and pre-bill claim validation. That stops recurring payer-specific denials at the source rather than reworking them one at a time. At a 400-bed hospital, this reduced coding-related denials by 75%.


### **4. Can hospitals outsource denial management without outsourcing the entire revenue cycle?**


Yes. Hospitals can engage providers for focused denial management, appeals, payer follow-up, or A/R recovery while retaining their existing billing teams. CombineHealth supports modular revenue cycle automation, allowing hospitals to automate specific workflows without replacing their complete RCM operation.


### **5. Does CombineHealth automatically categorize and prioritize denied claims?**


Yes. CombineHealth categorizes denials by payer, reason, dollar value, and aging, and prioritizes the claims with the highest recoverable impact — so teams work the denials that matter most first, and recurring reason codes feed back into prevention.


### **6. How does CombineHealth reduce recurring hospital denials?**


CombineHealth analyzes denial patterns and payer outcomes to identify recurring coding, documentation, eligibility, and billing issues. Validated findings inform future coding and claim-validation workflows. At a 400-bed hospital, CombineHealth reported a 75% reduction in coding-related denials.


### **7. How should hospitals measure denial management ROI?**


Hospitals should measure recovered cash net of vendor fees, denial rates, appeal overturn rates, appeal turnaround time, days in A/R, cost to collect, and repeat-denial rates. Tracking denial prevention separately from recovery helps determine whether the service is improving future claim performance.


### **8. How are denial management services priced?**


Common pricing models include contingency fees, fixed monthly fees, per-account pricing, per-FTE arrangements, and percentage-of-collections contracts. Pricing varies by claim volume, denial complexity, service scope, and operational responsibilities.


### **9. How quickly can denial management services produce results?**


Recovery may begin once claim data, payer access, and workflows are configured. Sustained denial reduction generally takes longer because recurring coding, documentation, and billing issues must be identified and corrected. Hospitals should request timelines for initial recovery and measurable denial prevention.
